verdict: FAIL (measured, no longer blocked) — INT-05 does NOT flip to PASS: three clauses of its own procedure are measured as unmet (playback does not federate, no per-remote-account block exists, remote URL resolves an actor but never a video). Source identity after migration stays MIG-06's.
headline: Two isolated Vidra instances federated for real over plain HTTP: signed Follow both ways with a measured approve/reject queue, Create/Update/Delete{Video} through a durable signed delivery queue, an inbound federated comment with its edit and its retraction, instance mute vs instance block proven to be different mechanisms, and the full 30s→60→120→240→480 retry ladder to a dead letter at attempt 6. Playback and posters do NOT federate: the outbound AS Video carries no icon, no duration and only a watch-page url, so a follower instance can store a card and link out and nothing else.

lab.scheme: plain HTTP; no TLS anywhere. Nothing in the code requires https — webFingerRemote tries https first and falls back to http whenever the SSRF relax is on, and PUBLIC_BASE_URL validation accepts an http origin.
lab.hostnames: NONE ADDED. /etc/hosts needs root and `sudo -n true` answered `sudo: a password is required`, so the two instances are distinguished by PORT and their fediverse domains are literally `127.0.0.1:18080` and `127.0.0.1:28080`. That works because every host comparison in the code reads url.Host, which carries the port: federation.hostOf/sameHost, Service.domain() for WebFinger matching, and instancemod.NormalizeDomain (which parses `https://`+domain and requires Host==domain). Nothing was added to or removed from /etc/hosts.

instance_a.core_worker: separate process, VIDRA_ROLE=worker (the federation delivery drain runs here)

lab.third_party_peers: three instances of a 200-line Go ActivityPub peer written for this lab (WebFinger + one Person actor with a keypair we hold + an inbox that logs): `hostile` on :38080 (killed mid-lab to be the permanently dead instance), `commenter` on :48080 (the remote commenter), `probe` on :58080 (an actor never cached, for the SSRF probe). They exist to send inputs a real Vidra instance cannot produce — unsigned, tampered, spoofed-actor, stolen-keyId.
lab.one_build_two_origins: ONE `next build`. lib/config.ts resolves the browser API base from the RUNTIME /runtime-config.js (PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL) and falls back to same-origin "" in production, so NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL was never baked and both frontends run the same standalone bundle with different INTERNAL_API_BASE_URL.
lab.proxy: one pipe-only Node proxy per origin that DROPS the client's Accept-Encoding. Core owns /api/, /.well-known/, /nodeinfo, /accounts/, /video-channels/, /inbox, /feeds, /sitemap.xml, /oembed, /healthz; everything else is the Next server.
lab.infrastructure: PostgreSQL 16.15 in its own cluster on 127.0.0.1:55433 (socket -k /tmp — the scratchpad path exceeds the 103-byte Unix-socket limit), Redis 8 on 127.0.0.1:56379, ffmpeg 6-second 640x360 fixture.

config.FEDERATION_KEY_KEK: base64 of 32 identical bytes — an obviously fake lab value, never committed
config.HTTP_IMPORT_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS: true on both — the relax the lab needed. It is the ONLY knob that lets urlsafety.Guard reach a loopback origin, and federation reads it through federation.WithAllowPrivateFetch(cfg.ImportAllowPrivateURLs). Turned OFF again for the SSRF probe.
config.JWT_SECRET: DELIBERATELY IDENTICAL on both instances, so that B's tokens answering 401 on A proves session isolation is a per-instance row and not an artefact of different secrets

publicKey.publicKeyPem: RSA SPKI PEM, minted lazily on first actor read and sealed at rest with FEDERATION_KEY_KEK

actor_shapes.account_actor: same shape, type Person, at /accounts/{username}; no attributedTo

video_object.name: title
video_object.url: http://127.0.0.1:18080/v/{short code} — a plain string, the human watch page
video_object.a08_watch_url_finding: RESOLVED and confirmed live. The AP object's `url` is /v/{short code}, not the unrouted /videos/watch/ of the original A08 finding, and its `id` stays /videos/{uuid} by design. The url answered 200 and really decoded in Chromium (640x360, 87 frames, 2 dropped, MSE blob).

sc1_discover_follow_accept_reject.follow_approval_policy: federation_follower_approval defaults FALSE — the shipped policy is AUTO-ACCEPT of an inbound channel Follow. federation_allow_channel_followers defaults true, federation_auto_follow_back false, federation_accept_remote_comments true. All four read live from the instance-settings overlay per inbound activity (a ~10 s settings poll, measured).
sc1_discover_follow_accept_reject.auto_accept: B viewerb POST /api/v1/me/remote-follows {handle: studioa@127.0.0.1:18080} → 201 pending at 08:01:21. WebFinger on A (https attempt then the http fallback), actor resolved and cached, signed Follow queued as viewerb's ACCOUNT actor, delivered, A auto-accepted and queued the Accept back signed as the CHANNEL actor, B flipped to accepted — the whole loop inside the first 5-second poll.
sc1_discover_follow_accept_reject.approval_queue: with federation_follower_approval on: otherb's Follow parked PENDING in A's GET /admin/federation/follower-requests carrying actor_url, handle otherb@127.0.0.1:28080 and domain; B still read pending. Approve → 204 → Accept delivered → B accepted within 5 s → A's queue empty.
sc1_discover_follow_accept_reject.reject: thirdb's Follow parked pending; A rejected → 204 → Reject delivered → B's remote-follow row DELETED (total 0) within 15 s; A's follower collection unchanged at 3.

signature_verification.logged: level=WARN msg=request method=POST path=/inbox status=401 with request_id and correlation_id

signature_verification.probe: validly signed, then ONE byte of the signature flipped (keyId, Date, Digest and the covered set all still valid)
signature_verification.logged: same WARN line with its own correlation id

signature_verification.probe: correctly signed Follow from the lab peer
signed by the peer but `actor` claims a user on B (acting on another actor's behalf)
signed by the peer but keyId claims B's viewerb key
signature_verification.cause: the resolved key is viewerb's real one and the signature does not verify against it

wrong_actors_on_the_approval_queue.note: both instances ran the SAME JWT_SECRET, so B's 401s on A are session isolation, not a signing mismatch

follower_counts.finding: the AP collection sums CountChannelFollowers + CountRemoteFollowers; the REST/UI count is CountChannelFollowers alone (`SELECT count(*) FROM channel_follows`), so the creator's own surfaces read ZERO followers while the actor document advertises three. Account collections are hard-coded empty by a documented decision in collections.go, so B's follower cannot be verified from its own `following` collection either.

sc2_video_lifecycle.verdict: PASS for delivery and lifecycle; the PLAYBACK clause fails and is recorded, not waived
sc2_video_lifecycle.create: A's creator published a 6-second fixture. One Create{Video} per distinct remote follower inbox (3), all delivered. B stored a metadata-only remote_videos row: object_url, remote_actor_url, title, description, watch_url=/v/{code}. duration_seconds NULL, stream_url NULL, thumbnail_key NULL.
sc2_video_lifecycle.what_B_stores: metadata only — by design (remote_videos has no media columns). B does not proxy and does not mirror bytes.
sc2_video_lifecycle.delivery_path_for_a_viewer_on_B: LINK-OUT ONLY. In Chromium: B's home feed at scope=all shows the card with a 'From 127.0.0.1:18080' origin badge and 'No preview'; /remote/{id} renders NO <video> element at all and says 'This video can't be played here. The origin instance did not provide a playable stream — use "Watch on 127.0.0.1:18080" below.' Following that link to A played for real: 640x360, readyState 4, duration 6.01 s, 87 frames, 2 dropped, blob: MSE source.
sc2_video_lifecycle.why_playback_does_not_federate: the ingest is READY for it — ingest.go's videoLinks() prefers an application/x-mpegURL link then a video/* link, iconURL() reads an Image, parseISODurationSeconds() reads PT6S — but the outbound videoObject() emits `url` as a bare string and no `icon` and no `duration`. So Vidra→Vidra federation can never populate stream_url, thumbnail_key or duration_seconds. A second wall sits behind it: A's media answers 200 anonymously but carries NO Access-Control-Allow-Origin, so an HLS master fetched cross-origin by hls.js would be blocked even if the link were emitted.
sc2_video_lifecycle.update: PATCH title+description on A → Update{Video} to all 3 inboxes → B's row reflected both fields within one 10-second drain.
sc2_video_lifecycle.delete: DELETE on A → Delete{Video} fanned out → B's remote_videos row GONE (count 0), GET /remote-videos/{id} 404, feed scope=all total 0, A's channel outbox totalItems 0.
sc2_video_lifecycle.remote_url_after_delete: A's core API answers 404 for the deleted video, but the AP object's `url` (/v/{code}) and its `id` path (/videos/{uuid}) both still answer HTTP **200** with the frontend shell that renders 'Video not found' client-side — the known soft-404 from the short-codes work, measured here from the federation side: a remote server dereferencing a retracted video's url gets 200.
sc2_video_lifecycle.private_and_unlisted_never_federate: a PRIVATE and an UNLISTED upload both reached state=published with a real HLS ladder on A and produced ZERO federation activities of any kind — the whole delivery ledger stayed at the public video's rows. AnnounceVideo/UpdateVideo gate on privacy=='public' AND state=='published'; UpdateVideo turns a video leaving that set into a Delete (unfederate).

sc3_comments.verdict: PARTIAL — inbound to the origin is complete; the reverse direction does not exist
sc3_comments.inbound: a signed Create{Note} from commenter@127.0.0.1:48080 whose inReplyTo was A's video object URL → 202 → stored and rendered on A as remote:true, author_username 'commenter', author_domain '127.0.0.1:48080', author_id null. Update{Note} edited it in place (edited:true). Delete{Note} removed it.
sc3_comments.delete_cascade: the Delete of the remote parent also removed the local creator's REPLY underneath it — comments.parent_id is ON DELETE CASCADE by design (migration 0026) and the local delete path is the same hard DELETE, so the federated Delete matches local semantics rather than exceeding them.
sc3_comments.outbound_from_a_follower_instance: DOES NOT EXIST. B's remote watch page deliberately offers no comment box ('Comments, ratings, and saving live on the origin instance'), and there is no API to author a comment against a remote video. federation.federateComment only fans a LOCAL comment on a LOCAL video out to that channel's remote followers.
sc3_comments.what_followers_do_with_an_inbound_commen: A's creator's local reply WAS fanned out as Create{Note} to all three follower inboxes and all three delivered — and B stored ZERO comments, because notes.go resolveNoteTarget requires inReplyTo to resolve to a LOCAL video. So a follower instance receives federated comments and drops every one; a remote video on B carries no comment thread at all.
sc3_comments.watched_words_over_remote_content: an inbound remote comment containing a watched term WAS flagged into A's moderation queue with its snapshot, offset and length — closing the A16-deferred facet. It also exposed a defect: the row named the LOCAL VIDEO OWNER as the author. Fixed TDD-first in vidra-core #200.

matrix.direct_read: GET /remote-videos/{id} still 200 — a muted instance's video stays reachable by direct URL
matrix.delivery: unaffected, content keeps arriving and is stored

matrix.inbound: an Update{Video} from the blocked origin was answered **202** and dropped — indistinguishable from acceptance at HTTP level, no audit row, no log line beyond the plain 202 request line, and NOT written to federation_inbox_activities
matrix.outbound: an Undo{Follow} to the blocked domain was dead-lettered immediately at attempt 1 with last_error 'cancelled: destination instance is blocked'
matrix.audit: one moderation.instance.block row, result success, reason 'domain=127.0.0.1:18080'
matrix.reversible: unblock restored feed and reads; a redelivery of the activity refused during the block was then accepted and applied

matrix.control: instance BLOCK against existing remote COMMENTS
matrix.effect: the blocked instance's already-stored comment vanished from the public comment list the moment the block landed, and the row stayed in the database (hidden, not deleted); unblock brought it back
feed 1→0 and the read 404 for everyone; unblock restored both
204; the report lands in B's moderation queue as target_type remote_video carrying remote_video_title and remote_video_domain — the A16-deferred remote-report facet, closed

DOES NOT EXIST. /me/mutes/accounts/{id} and /me/blocks/{id} take a LOCAL user UUID; a remote actor URL is 404 and muted_accounts.muted_id is a users FK. The finest granularity available against a remote person is blocking their entire instance.

sc4_blocks_and_mutes.follow_severance: NOT severed either way. Blocking A on B left viewerb's accepted follow row untouched. Worse, otherb's unfollow DURING the block deleted B's local row (local intent wins) while its Undo was cancelled — so A still counts otherb as a follower and kept delivering Create/Update/Delete to that inbox afterwards. A ghost follower with no path to correction.
sc4_blocks_and_mutes.lost_update: the Update refused during the block is never redelivered — A recorded it delivered (B answered 202) and the intermediate title edit is permanently missing on B. Only activities that arrive AFTER the unblock are applied.

sc5_remote_url_and_migration.verdict: PARTIAL — actor resolution works, video-URL resolution does not
sc5_remote_url_and_migration.handle_resolution: GET /videos/search?q=studioa@127.0.0.1:18080 on B returned remote:[{type:channel, actor:{actor_url, handle, domain}}] — the exact identity POST /me/remote-follows accepts. The actor URL form resolved identically.
sc5_remote_url_and_migration.video_url_resolution: FAILS against a Vidra origin. Searching the AP object id AND the /v/{code} watch URL both returned an empty result. Root cause: the object id is not dereferenceable as ActivityPub — GET /videos/{uuid} with Accept: application/activity+json answers HTTP 200 with the frontend's HTML, so fetchVideoObject cannot parse a Video and resolution degrades silently to local-only.
sc5_remote_url_and_migration.no_local_dedupe: B ALREADY held that exact object_url in remote_videos, and the search still did not find it: ResolveSearchTarget always attempts a network fetch and never consults GetRemoteVideoByObjectURL first. So the 'resolves and dedupes to the already-stored remote video' clause is unmet for a reason that has nothing to do with the store.
sc5_remote_url_and_migration.outbox_is_the_working_discovery_path: GET /video-channels/studioa/outbox?page=1 returned an OrderedCollectionPage whose orderedItems carry the FULL inline Create{Video} with the Video object — so a consumer CAN discover A's catalogue, just not by dereferencing an object id.
sc5_remote_url_and_migration.source_identity_after_migration: UNVERIFIED — MIG-06-dependent, and deliberately not faked. What it would need, stated precisely: (1) actor `id` continuity — the migrated instance must keep serving the SAME actor URLs, which means keeping the old domain or serving both, because remote_follows/remote_channel_follows/remote_actors/remote_videos are all keyed on the actor URL text and a changed origin orphans every edge; (2) key continuity — the RSA keypair must move with the actor or every remote's cached publicKeyPem stops verifying, and resolveRemoteActor never refreshes a cached actor (key rotation is explicitly a later slice), so a rotated key is a permanent verification failure at every peer that already cached it; (3) failing (1), a signed Move activity, which vidra neither sends nor handles — dispatchActivity has no Move arm, so an inbound Move is accepted-and-ignored. None of this was exercised: it needs the domain plan MIG-06 is blocked on.

sc6_outage_and_retry.schedule_from_code: internal/federation/deliver.go — deliveryBaseBackoff 30s doubling to a maxDeliveryBackoff of 6h, maxDeliveryAttempts 6, deliveryLeaseSeconds 300; drained by one goroutine per instance on a 10-second jittered ticker in batches of 20, claimed FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.
sc6_outage_and_retry.schedule_measured: with B's api stopped: attempts 1 → due in 30 s, 2 → 60 s, 3 → 120 s, 4 → 240 s, 5 → 480 s. Exactly deliveryBaseBackoff * 2^(attempts-1).
sc6_outage_and_retry.recovery: B's api restarted at 08:19:16; every pending delivery to B was delivered by 08:19:36 (inside one drain). B's remote_videos held ONE row carrying the title sent during the outage, and federation_inbox_activities held 10 rows for 10 distinct activity ids — no duplicate ingestion.
sc6_outage_and_retry.dead_letter: the peer on :38080 was killed at 08:17:08 and never came back. Its deliveries laddered 30→60→120→240→480 and reached state='failed' at attempts=6 by 08:34 — about 15.5 minutes of wall clock for the whole ladder. last_error is the transport error, truncated to 500 chars.
sc6_outage_and_retry.what_the_admin_sees: GET /admin/jobs carries a federation_deliveries queue with pending/running/done/failed counts and oldest_pending_age_seconds (measured: pending 1, done 25, failed 2, oldest 591 s). That is ALL: there is no per-delivery listing, no destination, no reason, and no retry or discard control; GET /admin/system has no federation component at all even with FEDERATION_ENABLED=true, and reported status ok throughout with two dead-lettered deliveries on the books.
sc6_outage_and_retry.correlation: federation deliveries carry no correlation id and write no job_runs rows — the A17 finding that six projected queues (federation among them) do not call the job recorder, confirmed here from the federation side.

ssrf_posture.relax_needed_for_the_lab: HTTP_IMPORT_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS=true, wired into federation via WithAllowPrivateFetch(cfg.ImportAllowPrivateURLs). Without it no loopback origin is reachable, so the lab could not run at all.

with_the_relax_OFF.result: 422 could not be resolved to a remote channel; NOTHING cached
422; the remote-URI search for the same handle also returned nothing

ssrf_posture.finding: the guard covers the FETCH, not the cache. resolveRemoteActor returns a cached remote_actors row before urlsafety.Guard ever runs, so a follow of an actor cached earlier (under the relax, or before an operator tightened the setting) proceeds without a guard check. Outbound delivery does re-validate — deliverActivity runs Guard.ValidateURL on the inbox URL every attempt — so the residual exposure is the cache read itself, not the outbound POST. The relax is also per PROCESS: flipping it on the api left the worker's deliveries unguarded until the worker was restarted too.

gaps_and_follow_ups.finding: playback and posters do not federate. The outbound AS Video emits no icon, no duration and a plain-string url, while the ingest parses all three, so every Vidra→Vidra remote video is a title, a description and a link-out. Emitting the HLS link additionally needs a CORS ruling for federated media (A's media carries no Access-Control-Allow-Origin), and adding duration/icon needs GetVideoByID and ListChannelOutboxVideos to carry duration and a thumbnail flag they do not have today — a sqlc change plus the AP golden fixtures, not a one-line edit.

the AP Video object id is not dereferenceable as ActivityPub. GET /videos/{uuid} with Accept: application/activity+json answers 200 with the frontend HTML because that path belongs to the frontend in both this topology and the shipped Caddy one. Consequences: handleAnnounce's fetch-the-object arm can never ingest from a Vidra origin, and remote-URI search for a Vidra video URL always fails. A fix needs a routing decision (content-negotiate /videos/* to core) as well as a core handler.
ResolveSearchTarget never consults the local remote_videos row by object_url before fetching, so a video B already stores cannot be found by pasting its URL.
a blocked instance's activity is answered 202 with no audit row and no log line, and an activity refused during a block is never redelivered after the unblock, so state silently diverges.
an unfollow whose Undo is cancelled by a destination block still deletes the local row, leaving the remote with a ghost follower it keeps delivering to, with no reconciliation path.
the REST/UI channel follower count excludes remote followers entirely (channel_follows only), so a creator with three federated followers reads zero everywhere except the ActivityPub collection.
there is no per-remote-account mute or block. The only account-granularity control against a remote person is blocking their whole instance.

a follower instance stores no federated comments at all — it receives Create{Note} for the videos it follows and drops every one, because the note's inReplyTo target is remote to it. Remote videos therefore carry no comment thread anywhere but the origin.
the AP object url of a DELETED video still answers HTTP 200 (the frontend soft-404), so a remote server dereferencing a retraction gets a page, not a 404.

federation deliveries write no job_runs rows and carry no correlation id; the admin sees only aggregate queue counts, with no per-delivery detail and no retry or discard control, and /admin/system has no federation component.
account actor collections (followers/following/outbox) are hard-coded empty by a documented decision, so a peer cannot verify a follow from the follower's own following collection.
resolveRemoteActor serves a cached actor without re-running the SSRF guard, and never refreshes a cached publicKeyPem — key rotation at a peer is a permanent verification failure here.

defects_fixed.title: the watched-word queue names the remote author of a federated comment
defects_fixed.was: ListWatchedWordMatches read COALESCE(cu.username, vu.username); a federated comment has user_id NULL so the row fell through to the VIDEO OWNER, and the moderation queue named an innocent local creator as the author of a remote actor's flagged words, with nothing saying the comment was remote
defects_fixed.now: COALESCE(cu.username, c.remote_author_name, vu.username) plus an additive author_domain (empty for local); the vu fallback stays because it is correct for a VIDEO match
defects_fixed.test: TestWatchedWordMatchNamesTheRemoteAuthorOnRealPG on real PostgreSQL, verified RED before GREEN

gates.vidra-core: make ci PASS (fmt-check, vet, migrate-lint, openapi-verify, sqlc-verify, test-race); go vet -tags=integration ./... clean; go test -tags=integration -count=1 -p 1 ./internal/store/... ./internal/federation/... ok on a FRESH database
gates.vidra-core_flakes: on a REUSED test database TestExpiredLeaseBecomesClaimableAgain and the owner-claim test failed; both pass in isolation on this branch AND on clean main, and both pass on a fresh database — lab artefacts of a shared database under load, not regressions
gates.vidra-user: NOT RUN — no vidra-user change was made
gates.meta: shell and compose gates NOT RUN — no script, compose or env file changed

not_run: TLS. The whole lab is plain HTTP; nothing verified vidra's behaviour behind real certificates, and no CA was trusted.

Real hostnames. /etc/hosts needs root, which was refused, so both fediverse domains are host:port literals. Nothing here proves behaviour with a DNS name, punycode, or a domain that differs from the listening host.
Interoperability with PeerTube or Mastodon. Every peer was vidra or the purpose-built lab peer, so the outbound documents are proven self-consistent, not accepted by another implementation.
S3 storage, CDN delivery, live, and IPFS — all off.
Search service. SEARCH_SERVICE_URL was empty, so vidra-search's own handling of federated rows was not exercised.
The federation e2e frontend suites (this repo's AGENTS.md forbids running them locally).
teardown: all four core processes, both frontends, both proxies, the three lab peers, the PostgreSQL cluster and the Redis server were started by this session in a scratch directory and stopped at the end; the two lab databases live only in that cluster. /etc/hosts was never touched. The instance-settings overrides made during the lab (federation_follower_approval) were reset to their defaults and both instance blocklists were emptied before teardown.
